question: Can the frozen extra-index configuration safely convert seven original acquisitions from Normal to Fast in the current viewer and reproduce exact interactive output and the reported 12.3 GB working set?

code.entrypoint: Live4DSTEM native AX Normal/Fast menu plus Tests/NativeUI/profile_seven_tilts.py trajectories

inputs.hash_definition: SHA256 of sorted shasum output covering all 28 original HDF5 master and shard files, including canonical paths

parameters.normal: existing paired ANS configuration without additional region indexes
parameters.fast: frozen interactive-speed: radial streams, compact offsets, trusted decode, core and ring fine indexes, exact compact events T192
parameters.memory: production admission budget, old resident retained until replacement ready; no headroom override
parameters.timing: native foreground full trajectories; positive drawable presentedTime, not kernel throughput or timer ticks
parameters.parity: full virtual-image hashes and exact DP switch/return; independent original-file reduction remains a required gate
parameters.cache: source files hashed immediately before launch; explicitly warm-source, not cold I/O

artifact_results.native-fast: 12.3085 GB resident; 114.0 all-seven ADF center, 90.6 ABF center, 117.5/118.5 resize updates per second. Exact preset maps, selected DP round trips and custom endpoints match Normal. One AX confirmation action returned an error despite delivery; failed attempt retained.
artifact_results.independent-maps: All seven full 262144-pixel uint32 ADF maps match independent bounded HDF5/NumPy UInt64 sums, with the four file-marked bad pixels excluded. No intermediate-trajectory oracle claim.
artifact_results.return-failure: Fast-to-Normal failed safely before replacing a resident: buffered encoding stage needed 3755163648 bytes but only 3673849856 additional bytes admitted. Superseded by bounded-return experiment.
